body.statement: The frozen panel is complete and aligned for same-date cross-sectional scoring: 177 rows with 59 observed dates per symbol from 2026-08-03 to 2026-10-30, common_dates (59) equal to union_dates (59), no symbol missing any observed-union date, and no duplicate keys or invalid/null closes, so at every observed date t all three symbols have a usable close; the observed union is not an exchange calendar, so absences from it are not proof of closures or suspensions.

citations.quote: All signal calculations use observations at/before t; execution no earlier than the next observed close.

body.statement: With lookback 5, the first five observed rows of each symbol are excluded for insufficient past observations (5 per symbol), leaving exactly 54 eligible signals per symbol; only 53 of those 54 have a next observed close because the last observed row (2026-10-30) has no later observation, so each symbol's final signal has no execution observation under the next-observed-close rule.

citations.quote: BaoStock historical unadjusted daily close, CNY/share. Current download, not a vintage archive.
Close-only jumps cannot identify corporate actions.

body.statement: Closes are unadjusted CNY/share and the score close[t]/close[t-5]-1 divides same-symbol closes, so currency and price level cancel and the score is a dimensionless simple return on a common scale across symbols, even though price levels differ by roughly two orders of magnitude (600000.XSHG closes 8.97-10.02 vs 600519.XSHG closes 1235.58-1392.05); the series is unadjusted and a current non-vintage download, and close-only jumps cannot identify corporate actions, so the specification carries no corporate-action adjustment.

citations.quote: Normalization divides the trailing return by trailing daily-return SD times sqrt(lookback); this does not make an annual Sharpe ratio or remove systematic risk.
No forward labels, PnL, alpha, formal evaluation or proof that a revision is better.

body.statement: Hypothesis: with normalization 'none', per-symbol score dispersion is unequal (score sample SD 0.03136 for 000651.XSHE vs 0.02601 for 600000.XSHG and 0.02504 for 600519.XSHG) even though the three symbols' one-observation return SDs are similar (0.01370, 0.01249, 0.01290), so realized-volatility normalization might place trailing 5-observation returns on a more comparable scale; this is unproven, such normalization is not an annual Sharpe ratio and does not remove systematic risk, and the frozen sources contain no forward labels, PnL or alpha, so no variant can be shown superior here.

Accepted as a supported units constraint. The change is deferred until evaluation evidence outside this bundle exists; normalization 'none' is retained.
